Rule 4, Paulo group ruling (paulo-group-ruling.tsv): Paulo group ruling: fragment, no user fact of its own
Old: ===================


New: WHAT DO I DO FIRST?
===================

You are at: Start | No project open

Start page. The family workflow and the optional de novo workflow stay available. Project: none open. File > Open opens a project. The navigation list keeps Families, Quantify, Results and De novo within reach.

Project: none open.

STEP 1 · Group the proteins into families
   Menu: File > New from database
   Needs: a protein database, either a plain .fasta or a target-decoy .T-R file.
   Produces: a Family Cluster File (.fcf) written next to the database.
   Choose database, set identity, then Build families. 85% is the initial value. "Scan
   identity range" shows how the family count and the target/decoy mixing behave
   across the whole range, which is a better basis for the choice than a single
   number. Find lowest identity uses Divide and Conquer to find the lowest identity
   with no mixing at all. That is a floor, not a recommendation. Help > How to read
   these numbers explains why.

STEP 2 · Open the families
   Menu: File > Open
   Needs: the .fcf from step 1.
   You can now merge families further by their description words, or build one family
   from a keyword list. Curation changes can be undone in this session. Use Save as
   to keep the previous grouping in a separate project.

STEP 3 · Attach the quantitation
   Open Quantify to compute or update full XIC for this project.
   In Families > Quantitation use Full XIC > Share of and Shared peptides.
   For the secondary source, open PatternLab (optional) and Load PatternLab project.
   PatternLab needs a project (.plp) exported at PEPTIDE level. A protein-level
   export contains nothing that can be attributed to a family, and every row will
   read 0.
   In PatternLab (optional), PatternLab share of chooses what the percentages are a
   share of. Choose what to do with peptides that belong to several families, then
   press Recalculate. Modes the project cannot support are greyed out, each with
   the reason in its own tooltip.

STEP 4 · Take the result away
   Export to CSV writes exactly the rows on screen, with the shares as fractions
   between 0 and 1 and a dot for the decimal separator, so any program can read them.
   File > Save keeps the project for next time. File > Export also writes families
   for FamilyQuant 1.5 (.fcf), preserving the grouping without stored quantitation.
   Analysis > Reannotate SEPro stamps your User ID family numbers into a copy of a SEPro
   result package, leaving the original untouched.

OPTIONAL · Review de novo evidence
   Menu: Analysis > De novo evidence
   A separate workflow, not a step of the four above. It changes no family, no User ID
   and no quantitation, and it needs no Family Cluster File to start. Use it to ask
   how the selected de novo calls relate to PatternLab. Its two core steps are:
     1. Select PEAKS or DeepNovo and keep calls passing all three filters: minimum
        length, the source-native score, and a consecutive local-confidence stretch.
     2. Compare them with a SEPro search of the SAME runs. Each kept row comes back
        as new territory, a co-isolated second species, a redundant confirmation, an
        agreement PatternLab itself scored weakly, or a straight disagreement. The
        last two are listed as a review queue, because they are decisions.
   Quantify provides extraction and Results reads the ion-current recovery. Family
   attribution remains available for de novo work without a saved project.
   That screen has a Help button of its own, and while it is open Help · How to read
   these numbers shows its page instead of this one.
